name: Ghana
sources: Inflation 37.3% in 1990 (Ghana Statistical Service CPI), up sharply from 25% in 1989 on drought and a cedi devaluation; Bank of Ghana rediscount rate around 33%. The Economic Recovery Programme of 1983 had taken the cedi from 2.75 to the dollar to over 300 by 1990, which is why a nominally market system shows a rate this high.

Defence 0.5% of GDP, one of the lowest ratios anywhere: Rawlings had cut the officer corps that produced the coups he himself had led in 1979 and 1981, and the army's foreign earnings came from UN peacekeeping rather than the budget.
Tax take 13% of GDP; cocoa duty through the Cocoa Marketing Board is the largest single line and cocoa prices were at a twenty-year low in 1990.

Authoritarianism 0.80 and stability 52: the Provisional National Defence Council had ruled by decree since 31 December 1981 with all parties banned. It was the IMF's showcase adjuster, which bought it stability an unelected government would not otherwise hold. District assembly elections held on a no-party basis from December 1988 were the transition's first step; the ban on parties lifted in May 1992.
Separatism 0.06: low. The Ewe question and Togoland irredentism exist but have never been armed at scale.
